cards.explanation: The answer is their gold earrings. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), tells them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.” (Exodus 32:2) Then all the people take off their gold earrings and bring them to Aaron (Exodus 32:3). That's a whole lot of jewelry heading in one direction, friends.

The answer is calf. Aaron takes the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashions it into a molten calf (Exodus 32:4). Gold earrings go in, and a calf comes out, friends. Then the people say, “These, O Israel, are your gods…”

The answer is an altar. When Aaron sees the calf, he builds an altar before it and proclaims, “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.” (Exodus 32:5) The next day they offer burnt offerings and present peace offerings. Things are moving fast down in that camp, friends.

The answer is True. The next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. Then “…the people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.” (Exodus 32:6) Offerings first, then the party. Notice the order, friends.

The answer is quickly. The LORD says, “How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them!” (Exodus 32:8) He lists it out: they made a molten calf, bowed down to it and sacrificed to it. Moses had been gone a while, but the turning aside happened FAST.

The answer is False. Right after “Now leave Me alone…” the text says Moses “…sought the favor of the LORD his God…” (Exodus 32:11) He speaks up and asks why the LORD's anger burns against His people. I think that's a man who really cares about the people he leads.

The answer is that Moses says the Egyptians would declare He brought them out to kill them in the mountains. Moses asks, “Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’?” (Exodus 32:12) Then he asks the LORD to turn from His fierce anger and relent from doing harm to His people. Moses is pleading for them, friends.

The answer is descendants like the stars and the land. Moses reminds the LORD of what He declared: “I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised, and it shall be their inheritance forever.” (Exodus 32:13) Moses brings up the promise itself. That's a man who knows what to hold onto, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, “So the LORD relented from the calamity He had threatened to bring on His people.” (Exodus 32:14) That comes right after Moses pleads for them and reminds the LORD of His promise to Abraham, Isaac and Israel. The calamity doesn't come, friends.

The answer is the sound of singing. Joshua hears the people shouting and says to Moses, “The sound of war is in the camp.” But Moses replies, “It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!” (Exodus 32:17-18) Joshua took the shouting for war, and Moses names it as singing. I think Joshua was about to get a very different kind of news.

The answer is False. When Moses sees the calf and the dancing, he “…burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain.” (Exodus 32:19) No handoff, no safekeeping, friends. The tablets were the work of God, and they break right there (Exodus 32:16).

The answer is drink. Moses burned the calf, ground it to powder and scattered the powder over the water. Then, the text says, “…he forced the Israelites to drink it.” (Exodus 32:20) It's a heavy moment, friends, and it shows how seriously Moses took what they had made.

The answer is evil, friends, and Aaron says it like he's reading the blame off a cue card. Moses asks how the people could have led him into so great a sin (Exodus 32:21). Aaron's first move is to say, “Do not be enraged, my lord…” and then he points at the crowd: “You yourself know that the people are intent on evil.” (Exodus 32:22) I think Aaron hopes that if everyone else is standing in the spotlight, nobody will look at him. I've tried that move myself.

The answer is False. Aaron repeats the people's request, then tells Moses, “And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!” (Exodus 32:24) He never mentions an engraving tool or fashioning it himself, friends. The earlier verse says he did use one (Exodus 32:4).

The answer is all the Levites. Moses stands at the entrance to the camp and says, “Whoever is for the LORD, come to me.” The text says, “And all the Levites gathered around him.” (Exodus 32:26) All of them came, friends.

The answer is True. Moses says to the Levites, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.” (Exodus 32:29) It comes after a heavy day, friends. I think this part of the story is hard to sit with.

The answer is to be blotted out of God's book. Moses says, “Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.” (Exodus 32:32) He puts himself on the line for the people. I think that tells you how much he cares for them, friends.

The answer is sinned. The LORD replies to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot out of My book.” (Exodus 32:33) It's His answer to Moses' request about being blotted out of the book. Then He tells Moses to go lead the people to the place He described, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you.” (Exodus 32:34) Moses is sent to lead the people, with the LORD's angel going before them. No waiting around on the mountain, friends. And the story isn't over yet.
